ko.executive_summary: SK Hynix aggressively pursues talent acquisition by removing educational barriers in new hiring and recruiting treasury experts from Seoul's financial sector, while seeking TSMC 3nm expertise. Meanwhile, Nvidia halts Southeast Asia server shipments amid U.S. export controls, and Nvidia/Kioxia explore alternatives to South Korean memory chips for AI servers.
key_facts: SK Hynix holding $61.5 billion in cash
SK Hynix eliminates educational degree requirements for new hires
Nvidia suspends AI server shipments to Southeast Asia
Nvidia and Kioxia partnering on alternative AI server memory

implications.text: Small chipmakers struggle to compete with nine-figure bonuses from Samsung and SK Hynix; U.S. semiconductor workforce talent gap persists despite recruitment efforts.
U.S. AI chip restrictions forcing Nvidia to halt regional shipments and spurring development of non-Korean memory alternatives.
SK Hynix's removal of degree barriers and financial sector recruitment signal aggressive capacity-building for AI/HBM growth.

ko.counterpoint: SK Hynix's large cash position and hiring breadth may not translate to immediate 3nm process capability gains versus TSMC.
